articles.title: Large Employers Gain Visibility Into PBM Collections From Drugmakers and Pharmacies
articles.summary: New transparency requirements are giving large self-funded employer health plans unprecedented visibility into the full scope of collections and revenues generated by pharmacy benefit managers from drugmakers and pharmacies. This increased transparency allows plan sponsors to better scrutinize PBM contracts, evaluate true net drug costs, and push for more favorable pricing models. For self-funded employers, this data represents a powerful tool to demand accountability and optimize prescription drug spending.
articles.source_line: Source: Medical Daily; Sat, 31 Oct 2026 00:46:47 GMT

articles.title: Large Employer Health Plans Face Changing PBM Rebate Dynamics
articles.summary: Recent analysis highlights evolving financial flows regarding pharmacy benefit manager rebates within large employer health plans. This shift directly impacts plan design, net cost management, and transparency for self-funded employers navigating drug spend. Understanding these rebate structures is critical for employers evaluating PBM contract terms and overall pharmacy benefit ROI.

articles.title: University of Kentucky Sues CVS Over Alleged 340B Drug Savings Diversion
articles.summary: The University of Kentucky has filed a lawsuit accusing CVS Caremark of diverting over $41 million in hospital drug savings generated through the 340B program. This high-profile legal battle highlights growing scrutiny over PBM and specialty pharmacy administrator handling of 340B revenues, a critical issue for self-funded plan sponsors and healthcare institutions navigating drug pricing transparency.
articles.source_line: Source: Medical Daily; Sat, 31 Oct 2026 13:46:46 GMT

articles.title: New Mandates Force Increased Business Disclosure for PBMs
articles.summary: New regulatory mandates are compelling pharmacy benefit managers to disclose complex business dealings and financial structures. This heightened transparency directly impacts self-funded employers by shedding light on spread pricing, rebates, and underlying contract terms. Plan sponsors can use these disclosures to better evaluate PBM performance and negotiate more cost-effective pharmacy benefits.
